payload.text: PROBE IN A SCRATCH COPY, NEVER THE SHARED TREE -- AND A SCRATCH REPO IS STILL A COMMIT. Both mine, 2026-09-23. (1) I planted a probe .md under the shared tree's lib/ for about a second to test a prettier ignore rule, after telling cc I would write nothing under lib/ that day. It was removed and lib/ verified clean; it should have been a run against a copy. (2) To make a partial-install fixture a repository, I committed in it with --no-verify, which hv's rule forbids on any commit, scratch and hook-less repos included; git init with an add, or an ordinary commit, would have served. Both were cheap to avoid, and nothing caught either but a re-read.
